entities.title: zazzle investigate --adaptive
entities.summary: The adaptive mode of `zazzle investigate` (`--adaptive`, `--agents`, `--orchestrator`, `--orchestrator-effort`, `--prose`, `--json`) and its review (`--review-model`, `--review-effort`) and benchmark (`--benchmark-model`, `--benchmark-effort`): each part of a question runs on the cheapest agent and effort that will do it, and an unsettled part goes up the ladder with what it established.
entities.purpose: mod.rs separates its flags from investigate's, builds the ladder (agent.rs: `MODEL`, `local:`, `claude:` or `codex:` specs, each `@EFFORT` or at low then high; by default the installed local models from `ai-agent status --json`, smallest first), rates the question 0 to 5 without a model, reads the task into items with ids and constraints (items.rs) and, above 0 with two items or more not all about one discovered component, asks a planner one rung above the difficulty to assign item ids to at most four `PART agent | I1,I2 | symbols` lines, held to a grammar when local and checked before dispatch (more than four parts is refused, so no assigned item goes unrun) with one repair that shows the planner its refused plan (a refused repair runs the task as one assignment) (a planner that fails, gives no parts, rates its understanding low or asks to escalate is replaced by the next rung once). The parts run at the same time, each on its rung and with its own read session (calls.rs `all`, one thread per part): a local rung through investigate's lookup loop (explore and work, with --context for what an earlier attempt established), a hosted rung as one read-only `claude -p` or `codex exec` call whose reply lines are parsed and whose citations are checked (work.rs). A part escalates on a failure, a request to escalate, a low rating, rejected citations only or nothing verified, at most three times, never past the top or the time limit, and never when it is blocked on the user. A benchmark gets a reviewer by default, the strongest agent the machine can run (claude:opus at high effort when claude is installed, else the strongest hosted rung, else the strongest local one; --no-review leaves it out). The reviewer, with a benchmark, gets the wall-clock seconds, calls, tokens and cost zazzle measured for both results and must compare them on each of quality, time and tokens; one it leaves out is reported as not compared. With --orchestrator (any agent spec, usually claude: or codex:) it alone plans, with no ladder planner after it, combines and writes the --prose summary; otherwise the planner combines and the cheapest rung summarizes. The combiner writes the answer from the parts' findings by id (lines marked supported, inference, proposal or unknown; an unknown id, an unsupported claim or a widened citation is refused), keeps every part's findings and gaps (an escalated part's earlier findings too), skips the call when nothing was verified, falls back to the findings when it fails, and holds the task's word limit with one retry, then a cut. One deadline set when the job is accepted bounds it all: the main run (with a hosted benchmark beside it), a local benchmark and the review each end by their share of the time left, no part, escalation or model call starts after the deadline (calls.rs refuses it), and every report ends with the usage per role, an `orchestration` JSON object listing every step with its agent and tokens in and out, the orchestrator's apart from the delegated agents', and each adaptive run appends a text-free record to the orchestration log (record.rs). Calls that reported no token counts stay unknown in the usage, never zero, and a sink appends each call's usage to the job's run as it ends. items.rs reads the task into items, context and constraints: list lines, inline numbers `(1) ..; (2) ..`, or question sentences are items; a sentence that names a machine path, the workspace or zazzle, or starts with an instruction on how to work (use, do not, run, reply, return ..), is a constraint, never subject; the subject (context and items) is what discovery, the planner's leads and the one-component check rank code by. When planning is skipped or the repaired plan is refused, one part keeps every item by id with the context and the constraints (one item keeps the prompt as given), and the planner's refusals are kept in the JSON result (`plan.notes`) and counted in the log. After every attempt coverage.rs checks each of the part's items against everything verified so far, from the files: an item needs a verified finding in one of the files discovery ranks best for it (at least half the best score) or, elsewhere, one naming two of its terms; a document never counts and a citation about no item is listed as unrelated; tests need a finding in test code, callers a finding in another production file that uses the type or the interface it implements, a trace each call on a field in its cited lines followed to a body in another file (an interface member does not count; calls to code outside the scope and plumbing such as logging are left out), and a route the controller's class-level prefix cited. An item left open makes the result partial and escalates it however sure the agent was, with the lookups zazzle chose (the implementation and, two calls deep, what it calls; the interface's references; the test classes; the route line) run before the next attempt's first turn, the earlier lookups passed as tried (one that found nothing, or a file whose citations were unrelated, is not run again) and a different file read first by discovery; at the top of the ladder the same agent is asked once more while those lookups are new and it verified something. The result's JSON carries each item's coverage, the unrelated citations and per attempt the diagnostics (subject terms, ranked candidates with what they matched, each lookup with how its FIND was read and whether it found something, the stop reason); the orchestration log keeps only counts.
boundaries: Read-only: hosted agents run with Read, Grep and Glob only (claude, dontAsk) or a read-only sandbox (codex); local rungs use investigate's read-only lookups.
Only citations are checked, never claims; the report says the claims are the models'.
Hosted agents run only when --agents, --review-model or --benchmark-model names them; nothing is downloaded.

Local calls share daemon's one worker, so local parts take turns on it (a local part waits for the job's local turn and keeps it for all its calls, so its prompts follow each other and reuse their prefix in the worker) while hosted parts run beside them; the dedicated threads keep minutes-long agent calls off daemon's CPU pool.
Coverage is checked from the files and the outline, never from the models' claims; it can ask for more evidence but never marks a claim true.
